svg.title: Distinguish a delayed transition from faster cell production
svg.desc: A simplified ordered control map considers growth and DNA integrity before replication, replicated material before mitosis, and chromosome attachment/tension before sister separation. Downward branches indicate that detected problems can delay progression or lead to other responses. These are regulatory processes, not organelles or exhaustive molecular checkpoints. An explicit qualitative observation of many aligned cells with little total-count change supports delayed progression as one possibility. Comparing untreated populations, cell loss and completed divisions over time helps test it. Stage accumulation alone does not diagnose cancer or identify the molecular defect.

g.text: Distinguish a delayed transition from faster cell production
Cell-cycle controls coordinate events; a stage count is an observation, not a mechanism.
Detected problems can delay progression or lead to other responses.
Checkpoint names describe regulatory processes, not visible organelles.
Observation: many cells have aligned chromosomes; total cell count changes little.
Possible explanation: a delay before separation, rather than faster cell production.
Compare untreated cells over time; count cell loss and completed divisions too.
Stage accumulation alone does not identify the exact defect or diagnose cancer.
